about: Numbers the law payments use (src/core2/law-reach/law-payments.ts): SNAP's benefit formula and how a state's unemployment benefit fraction becomes a share of weekly pay. Each is tagged SOURCED (with citation), ESTIMATED (with source and spread) or TUNABLE (with the spread it's checked against).

snapGrossIncomeLimitShareOfPoverty.source: 7 U.S.C. 2014(c): a household's gross income may not exceed 130 percent of the poverty line.

snapBenefitReductionRate.source: 7 U.S.C. 2017(a): the allotment is the maximum less 30 percent of the household's net income.

snapEarnedIncomeDeduction.source: 7 U.S.C. 2014(e)(2)(B): 20 percent of earned income is deducted.

snapStandardDeductionSmallMinor.source: USDA Food and Nutrition Service, SNAP fiscal year 2026 cost-of-living adjustments: standard deduction for households of 1 to 3 in the 48 states and D.C., $209 a month.

snapStandardDeductionLargeMinor.source: USDA Food and Nutrition Service, SNAP fiscal year 2026 cost-of-living adjustments: standard deduction for households of 4 to 6 in the 48 states and D.C., $223 to $299 a month; the middle figure ($261, five people) stands for them.

snapLargeHouseholdFrom.source: 7 U.S.C. 2014(e)(1): the standard deduction rises for households of four or more.

snapMinimumBenefitMinor.source: USDA Food and Nutrition Service, SNAP fiscal year 2026 cost-of-living adjustments: minimum benefit for households of one or two, 8 percent of the one-person maximum, about $24.

snapMinimumBenefitMaxSize.source: 7 U.S.C. 2017(a): the minimum benefit applies to households of one or two.

highQuarterWeeks.source: A calendar quarter is 13 weeks: a benefit stated as a fraction of high-quarter wages is that fraction times 13 weeks of pay.

twoQuarterWeeks.source: Two calendar quarters are 26 weeks: a fraction of two quarters' wages is that fraction times 26 weeks of pay.

basePeriodWeeks.source: A base period is four calendar quarters, 52 weeks: a fraction of base-period wages is that fraction times 52 weeks of pay.

centsPerDollar.source: U.S. currency; the core keeps money in cents (minor units).
